label: PF Backlog 679
title: Delivery state and RCCA gate
body: Add explicit Code/Integration/Validation/Quality/Delivery Complete states, Gate 2 consumption and RCCA requirement for escaped defects.

brief.why: Add explicit Code/Integration/Validation/Quality/Delivery Complete states, Gate 2 consumption and RCCA requirement for escaped defects.

acceptance_criteria: delivery_state_check reports missing states and blocks Delivery Complete until all prior states pass.
Gate 2 completion consumes delivery-state evidence, and escaped defects require RCCA with a linked backlog item.
evidence:
Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=046e0eced068
BLOCKER:
  - CL-015 violation: AC evidence entries (`ac_evidence`, `traceability`) cite only `docs/IMPLEMENTATION-CONTROLS-DESIGN.md` with no candidate SHA; empty SHA is incomplete, so Gate 2 cannot validate evidence.
  - Acceptance criteria are truncated mid-clause ("all prior s", "require RCCA with "); the verifiable pass/fail condition for AC-1 and AC-2 is undefined, blocking objective gate evaluation.
  - Design guardrail checklist (items 1-10) is entirely unanswered; per CL-008 the design must address reversibility, authz boundary, blast radius, invariants, and reuse before Gate 1.5 — approval is invalid while unaddressed.
MAJOR:
  - `affected_components` / `affected_files` are "Not specified", so the language rule (new shipped logic -> Go) cannot be confirmed and single-writer ownership (CL-001) cannot be verified.
  - Traceability maps FR-1/FR-2 "design", "test", and "evidence" all to the same design document; no fail-able test artifact or test file is declared (guardrail 6), so AC verification is unprovable.
  - `out_of_scope`, `risks`, and `affected_files` are "Not specified"; failure matrix covers only one case (`EVIDENCE_MISSING`) while AC-2's RCCA-with-backlog-link path has no stated failure behavior.
  - Dependency BI-PF-1540 is asserted but its status/contract is undefined; blocked-on-dependency behavior for `delivery_state_check` is unstated.
MINOR:
  - Rollback is generic "Revert the change" with no migration-interrupted or partial-application recovery path (guardrail 6).
  - Observability is reduced to "tests"; no minimum log/metric emission for gate denial is specified (guardrail 10).
  - Reuse check absent: no statement that `delivery_state_check` reuses existing gate owners/ports rather than duplicating state logic (CL-001).
  - `config_contract` claims "no new config on develop" but the state list ("all five states") is hardcoded-eligible with no single source of truth identified.
NIT:
  - FR titles are truncated in `design_pack.requirements` to match the clipped AC text; clean wording would improve review readability.
  - `spec_pack.rollback_dr` marked N/A while `functional_spec.rollback` exists; slight inconsistency in rollback coverage labels.
SUMMARY:
  - Design is a template-level stub: truncated ACs, unspecified files/ownership, and evidence unpinned to a SHA mean Gate 1.5/CL-015/CL-008 conditions are unmet.
  - Top risks: unverifiable AC-1/AC-2 acceptance, no fail-able test artifact, and unanswered security/reversibility guardrails.
  - Recommend returning to design (G1.5 PENDING) before any approval; scope itself (delivery-state + RCCA gate) is coherent and appropriately split.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=302a5f2f20f6
BLOCKER:
  - FR-2/Gate 2 integration is untested: no test exercises `gate2_completion_check.completion_gaps` with `delivery_states`/escaped-defect RCCA input, so AC-2 ("Gate 2 consumes delivery-state evidence") is implemented but not demonstrably fail-able.
MAJOR:
  - `rcca.linked_item` is only checked for non-emptiness; any string passes. AC requires a *linked backlog item* — the check never resolves it via `backlog`, so a bogus link satisfies the gate.
  - No call site/CI wiring in the diff shows `delivery_state_check` blocking the Delivery Complete transition itself; only Gate 2 imports `problems()`, so the "blocks Delivery Complete" half of AC-1 has no demonstrated enforcement point.
MINOR:
  - Redundant logic: the `delivery_complete without <state>` branch re-detects conditions already reported by the first `STATES` loop, producing duplicate/noisy problem entries instead of one authoritative message.
  - `except Exception` around the `delivery_state_check` import converts any failure (path, syntax, signature) into a gap string with no traceback/logging — fail-closed but poor diagnosability for a gate.
  - The wrapper test re-loads `tests/test_delivery_state.py` via `importlib` and copies functions into `globals()`; fragile symbol-by-name mirroring that silently drops non-`test_` fixtures/helpers the source may later rely on.
NIT:
  - Module docstring cites BI-PF-1538 rather than the shipping item BI-PF-1545, weakening change traceability.
  - `STATES` is hard-coded in the script with no shared owner/config registration, so a future state-order change must be edited in multiple places.
SUMMARY:
  - The delivery-state predicate and Gate 2 hook are present and fail-closed, and tooling Python satisfies the language rule.
  - Top risks: AC-2 has zero tests at the Gate 2 boundary, RCCA `linked_item` is not validated as a real backlog reference, and nothing in the diff demonstrates an active block on the Delivery Complete transition.
  - Recommend adding a Gate 2 integration test, resolving `linked_item` through `backlog`, and showing the enforcement call site before merge.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present
